title: Nadia Beller, Ex-Partner of Cerimedo, Leaves Bolivia Bound for Mexico. She Is Granted Safe Conduct
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by[SinEmbargo
Staff](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/) originally appeared in the
[November 11, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4902116/nadia-beller-expareja-de-
cerimedo-deja-bolivia-rumbo-a-mexico-le-dan-salvoconducto/), a Mexican
independent digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, November 11 (SinEmbargo).—** The authorities of **Bolivia**
authorized this Wednesday the **safe conduct** so that activist and lawyer
**Nadia Beller** , ex-partner of Argentine consultant [**Fernando
Cerimedo**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/fernando-cerimedo/), can leave the
country and travel to Mexico, after the Mexican Government granted her
diplomatic asylum in view of the risk she reported to her safety.

Through a statement, the **Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bolivia** reported
that, after concluding the evaluation of the request submitted on November 4
by the [**Embassy of Mexico**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4901011/nadia-beller-
pieza-fundamental-del-caso-cerimedo-se-asila-en-la-embajada-de-mexico/), the
competent authorities decided to grant the document. The decision was
officially communicated to the Mexican mission yesterday; however, the safe
conduct was delivered early this morning.

> "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in coordination with the Ministry of
> Government and the General Directorate of Migration, accompanied the
> corresponding procedure, with Mrs. Beller Delgadillo's departure from the
> national territory having taken place during the morning of this Wednesday,"
> reads the
> [document](https://x.com/MRE_Bolivia/status/2120452325680484737?s=20).

> [Post by @MRE_Bolivia on
> X](https://twitter.com/MRE_Bolivia/status/2120452325680484737)

The Bolivian nation stated that the procedure was carried out in accordance
with its legal system and its international obligations, in addition to
reaffirming its willingness to maintain relations of dialogue, cooperation and
mutual respect with Mexico.

## Beller Reported Police Harassment

Before entering the Mexican Embassy in La Paz, Beller reported that the police
officers assigned to guard her did not offer her guarantees of safety and, on
the contrary, harassed her and restricted her freedom of expression.

In an interview with the Bolivian outlet _DTV_ , she explained that she
decided to seek protection on her own after requesting that the officers
withdraw from her home. According to her account, she submitted that request
on October 29, but the Prosecutor's Office resolution to withdraw the guard
was not issued until October 30 and was carried out on November 3.

Beller was the victim of an armed attack on August 17, 2026, when **two men
disguised as delivery workers shot her** outside the Hotel Swiss Contact, in
Santa Cruz de la Sierra. The activist was hit by three bullets and survived
after being taken to a hospital.

One day after the attack, the Bolivian Police arrested Fernando Cerimedo at
the Viru Viru international airport, when he was trying to board a flight
bound for Buenos Aires. The courts imposed 180 days of pretrial detention on
him, after he was charged as the alleged mastermind of the attack,
investigated as attempted femicide.

After being discharged from the hospital, Beller reported that the aggression
was aimed at silencing her and requested to enter the Victims and Witnesses
Protection Program. She also pointed out alleged irregularities during her
hospitalization.

![Fernando Cerimedo with Donald Trump Jr., Brad Parscale and Dick
Morris](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/2026-11-11-beller-safe-conduct-02-cerimedo-trump-
jr.jpg)From left to right: Andy Rivas (back turned), Fernando Cerimedo, Donald
Trump Jr, Brad Parscale and Dick Morris. Photo: Nadia Beller

The activist has provided information to the Argentine Federal Prosecutor's
Office about an alleged **network of bribes and diversion of funds in the
National Disability Agency (ANDIS)** , during the Milei administration. Her
statements have also addressed the alleged use of troll farms, disinformation
campaigns and the financing of _influencers_ in various countries of Latin
America.

In Bolivia, her complaints gave rise to investigations and raids in La Paz,
where large amounts of cash, official vehicles and satellite phones were
seized, as part of an inquiry that also involves officials of the government
of President Rodrigo Paz.
